profiles.configuration: 930E-5 chassis brochure AESS921-01, a configuration reference within the broader 930E AHS family. Not a bill of materials for every AHS conversion or 930E-5AT. Drivetrain controls and maintenance telemetry are separate from the FrontRunner autonomy computer.

facts.details: Komatsu SSDA16V160 16-cylinder diesel, 2,014 kW gross; GTA-51 alternator and GDY106-B induction wheel motors. Emissions configuration varies by market.
Invertex IIe AC control with independent rear-wheel motor control and air-cooled IGBT inverters; controller CPU not named.
CENSE monitors cylinder-level engine performance.
KOMTRAX Plus 2 uses satellite communications for machine metrics and faults; this is not the AHS fleet-control radio.
Ground-access service center, starter/drive isolation switches and emergency engine shutdown.

profiles.configuration: AutoMine Lite version 2, TS9-002:04/ENG, 2019. This is a specific single-machine loader/truck automation package, not every AutoMine generation or vehicle. Basic/Silver/Gold features vary; CPU, memory and storage SKUs are not disclosed.

facts.details: InfraFREE navigation, safety, network and video/audio modules; interfaces to VCM or SICA machine controls. Centralized or distributed enclosure layouts.
Four cameras, two laser scanners, articulation and bucket/boom sensors. Gyroscope and surface navigation are optional.
2.4 GHz 802.11 b/g/n; alternatively LTE Category 4. Requires 10 Mb/s per machine and maximum 100 ms latency. No unique SSID pattern is given.
Onboard package uses 24 VDC; mine-side supply requires 110–240 VAC, 50/60 Hz. Vehicle propulsion depends on the loader/truck.
IP network with Ethernet/fiber backbone; optional SQL reporting view. Access barriers and fast-stop controls isolate the production area.
Remote Supervisory System plus onboard InfraFREE; autonomous tramming/dumping and assisted teleoperation, depending on package.

profiles.configuration: July 2025 LinkOA for Haulage architecture. Retrofit equipment varies by truck. CPU, RAM, disk, radio model and supply ratings are undisclosed; do not inherit a host truck engine or newer kit into historical Mobius installations.

facts.details: Local processor interfaces with vehicle systems; part number unspecified.
GPS/GNSS, radar, lidar and additional obstacle-detection sensors; exact sensor models vary or are unstated.
Drive-by-wire operates steering, braking and throttle. Separate APIs connect upstream applications and vehicle interfaces; staffed vehicles use an In-Cab Client.
LinkOA traffic management routes mixed fleets, coordinates vehicles and can supply fleet-management functions. Vehicle Automation Kit and drive-by-wire execute onboard control.
Epiroc renamed ASI Mining’s Mobius surface-autonomy solution LinkOA in September 2024.

profiles.configuration: Legacy ASI Mining software/platform reference, not one physical truck. Current LinkOA hardware is documented separately; no CPU, memory, RF module or sensor list is established for every historical Mobius installation.

facts.details: Mobius can operate independently or integrate with ASI Nav and Vantage automation components.
Remote supervision, repeated loading/dumping assignments, vehicle diagnostics and multi-truck operation from one operator station.
Epiroc’s September 2024 announcement renames the acquired ASI Mining surface-autonomy solution LinkOA.

profiles.configuration: Pit Viper 271 brochure 9863 0005 01, July 2018. A documented variant of the catalog’s unspecified Pit Viper family; not the 271 XC, 291 or 271 E. Automation and engine/motor options are alternatives, not universally fitted. CPU/RAM/storage and wireless bands are unstated.

facts.details: Standard RCS CAN-bus control architecture with touchscreen, joysticks and safety interlocks; processor SKU unspecified.
RCS monitors penetration, torque, pressure, feed force and depth. Optional GPS hole navigation supports drill plans and installation-dependent ±10 cm accuracy.
CAT C27: 652 kW; CAT C32: 708 kW; Cummins QSK23 Tier 2: 641 kW. Electric options: WEG 6808 at 522 or 671 kW, or WEG 6811 at 671 kW; frequency/configuration restrictions apply.
Wireless remote tramming and Rig Remote Access file transfer; no radio standard or channel specified.
Hydraulic tracked drive, rotary head and four leveling jacks; Common Communications Interface exchanges RCS data.
Autodrill, Autolevel, BenchREMOTE, teleremote operation and Desktop Viewer are configuration-dependent add-ons.

profiles.configuration: Pronto product family under Atoms Mining, with February 2026 Vision, VLR and VLR 360 editions. Sensor suites differ; no common CPU, memory, radio chipset, battery or truck engine is disclosed. A retrofit does not identify the underlying truck model.

facts.details: Vision uses HDR cameras; VLR adds long-range lidar and radar; VLR 360 expands to full-perimeter sensing. The earlier solution reference also documents GNSS.
Wireless connectivity is required; Pronto describes Pollen Mobile private LTE as an available mine-network solution, not mandatory hardware on every truck.
Retrofit drive-by-wire kit; manually operated interacting equipment receives all-stop controls.
Demonstrated routes are saved for dispatch from the mobile app, which shows vehicle location and operating metrics; OTA software updates supported.
Pronto identifies itself as the technology core of Atoms Mining after acquisition.

profiles.configuration: Zyfra/VIST authors’ 2020 engineering paper describes the tested BELAZ 7513 architecture underlying the serial 7513R. These are reference-design components, not a guarantee for every production revision. CPU silicon, RAM, disk, radio bands and exact engine are undisclosed.

facts.details: KB-01 (КБ-01) executes autonomous and remote-control software and exchanges information with actuation, diagnostics and safety subsystems.
Diagram shows 3D surrounding lidar, side-view 2D lidar, radar, ultrasonic sensors and remote-view cameras; navigation and communication antennas are separate.
High-speed wireless exchange between onboard and operator equipment; protocol and frequency are not identified.
Actuator and diagnostic subsystems plus separate emergency-stop subsystem; handheld remote and onboard stops are shown.
The tested 110–130 tonne vehicle design uses AC/DC electromechanical transmission; no specific engine model is established.
Zyfra documents 7513R autonomous routes and unloading, fleet/loading coordination, mapped monitoring and remote fallback.

profiles.configuration: South Pit deployment architecture described by EACON executives in a December 2023 manufacturer-hosted interview. This does not specify every EACON truck or later ORCA revision. CPU, RAM, sensor SKUs, radio bands and battery capacity are unpublished in the source.

facts.details: Onboard edge computers handle perception, path planning, decisions and vehicle coordination; central servers handle dispatch and map management.
Multi-sensor fusion and onboard video; detailed sensor types and part numbers are not provided.
LTE/5G mine network and vehicle-to-vehicle communications; staffed vehicles carry positioning and communication devices.
Drive-by-wire and a platform interface separate autonomy from chassis systems across OEM truck models.
Deployment was transitioning from diesel trucks to hybrid-electric trucks; the account is not a single powertrain specification.
Vehicles send processed status and fault information; maps use differential updates. Dispatch provides 3D views, statistics and fleet reporting.

profiles.configuration: 2018 engineering concept, slide 22, supplemented by the current manufacturer AHS overview. Historical component blocks are not a current production BOM. CPU, memory, radio bands and sensor SKUs are undisclosed; no exact truck engine or battery is inferred.

facts.details: Separate AHS controller and electric steering controller; processor silicon not identified.
GNSS, IMU, lidar and radar appear in the retrofit architecture.
2018 design shows wireless communication; current AHS overview describes a dedicated communications network for remote-stop safety controls, without specifying its radio standard.
AHS add-on interfaces with the truck’s electric steering and AC motor-control systems.
Wenco Fleet Management System coordinates operations; current AHS supports instrumented staffed trucks and open FMS/AHS interoperability.

profiles.configuration: T 264 diesel chassis reference plus the Liebherr/Fortescue AHS program. The fleet record does not resolve the installed engine option. Keep separate from T 264 Battery Electric; CPU, memory, radios and autonomy sensor part numbers are not disclosed.

facts.details: Cummins QSK 60 standard; Liebherr D9812 or MTU 16V4000 optional, each rated 2,013 kW. Litronic Plus AC drive uses IGBT technology; payload class 240 tonnes.
Joint Liebherr/Fortescue AHS development includes fleet management and machine guidance; four T 264 trucks entered onsite validation. The management tools also support human-operated sites.

profiles.configuration: Separate Bauma 2025 battery-electric demonstration configuration. The article states a battery power figure, not a verified energy capacity; no kWh rating is inferred. CPU, memory and sensor/radio part numbers remain undisclosed. This is not the diesel T 264 specification.

facts.details: Fortescue Zero battery replaces the combustion engine. Demonstrated charging technologies include a 6 MW static robotic charger and lateral Liebherr Power Rail dynamic charging.
Liebherr/Fortescue AHS with energy management to monitor fleet charge, coordinate charging and optimize vehicle routes and speeds; described as ongoing development in April 2025.

profiles.configuration: HxGN Autonomous Mining is a portfolio, not one vehicle. 2022–2023 platform references identify system modules but not CPU, RAM, storage, radio bands, sensor models or vehicle propulsion. Driver-assistance installations are not automatically fully autonomous.

facts.details: HxGN Autonomous Mining combines Power of One hardware with the Core computing platform; CPU model unspecified.
Power of One describes an onboard computer, antenna and display integrating sensors, field applications and cloud software.
Portfolio includes perception, path planning, machine intervention and drill automation. Mission Manager coordinates fleet/traffic movements and integrates with fleet-management and analytics tools.

profiles.configuration: SMODBV1 integration manual v1.0. These are radio-module components, not the processor or complete BOM of an aircraft, controller or dock. No numerical memory capacity or complete module power budget is disclosed.

facts.details: Connector pinout identifies QCA6174A; another supply row abbreviates it as QCA617A. This identifies the connectivity IC, not the host application processor.
SkydioLink dual-band radio with two IPEX u.FL 20441-001E-01 antenna connectors.
Two Hirose DF30FC-40DP-0.4V board connectors, spaced 38.44 mm; mating DF30FC-40DS-0.4V. J9800 carries power, four-bit SDIO, command, clock and enable signals.
Shielding doubles as heat spreader; installation requires a thermal connection such as a graphite strap to the host chassis.
Host factory configuration and GPS-based region handling govern radio frequency and power.

profiles.configuration: Gen 3 integration guide v1.1, January 2025, for 2ATQRSMODBV3 only. Does not establish the SMODBV3S revision, host CPU, module chipset, memory capacity or numerical supply requirements.

facts.details: Approved antenna table covers 2.4 and 5 GHz sub-bands; four IPEX u.FL 20279-001E-03 connectors. External N-type antennas are installation-dependent, not standard on every host.
Two Hirose FX12B-60P-0.4SV connectors; J3000 carries host power and control. The guide prints a truncated mating-part designation, so no full replacement part is inferred.
Shielding serves as a heat spreader with a thermal path to the host chassis, for example a graphite strap.
Factory host software sets permitted operating frequency and power; end-user modification is not provided.

profiles.configuration: SkydioLink integration manual for 2ATQRSMO5GV1. The contributed index associates this identifier with C78 Controller, but this profile describes the radio module only. Host CPU, RAM, storage and complete controller hardware are not established here.

facts.details: J9800 pinout explicitly names QCA6174A; the 3.3 V row shortens the label to QCA617A.
SkydioLink 5 GHz module, FCC 2ATQRSMO5GV1 and ISED 25280-SMO5GV1.
5 V supply for RF front ends, at least 780 mA; 3.3 V for switcher/radio and 1.8 V radio supply. These are module rails, not a host battery specification.
J9800 provides four data lines, SDIO command and clock, plus Wi-Fi enable.

profiles.configuration: Telit FN990A40, original RI7FN990A40 and electrically unchanged Skydio relabel 2ATQRA40. Standard A40 product brief; A28 and HP variants excluded. Module capabilities do not establish features enabled in every Skydio host. Memory capacities and aircraft processors are undisclosed.

facts.details: Skydio and Telit authorization letters identify Telit FN990A40, not Fibocom. Change of FCC identifier preserves the original electrical hardware.
Qualcomm Snapdragon X65. The X62 listed for FN990A28 is a different variant.
5G sub-6 GHz SA/NSA, FDD/TDD, Release 16; LTE Category 20 and 3G fallback. Supported bands and network configuration require the regional module specification.
gpsOne Gen 9 L1 GNSS; dedicated or shared RF path. This is module capability, not a verified aircraft navigation configuration.
Nominal 3.3 VDC; not the host vehicle battery voltage.
M.2, 30×52×2.25 mm; PCIe Gen 3 one lane, USB 3.1 Gen 2 and 1.8/3 V SIM. Four cellular antenna connections plus GNSS.
FOTA updates, Windows/Linux drivers and SGP.22 eSIM support.

profiles.configuration: December 2024 Platform 2 configuration, FCC 2BML6P2EV1-0. Radio module only; no P2 flight processor, memory, battery or newer P2EV3 computer assignment. Chip capabilities must not override the later host-specific disabled functions.

facts.details: Intel AX210D2W, relabeled from PD9AX210D2 with Intel authorization; not an aircraft application CPU.

December 17 change request restricts this configuration to 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi: Bluetooth and 5 GHz are disabled in software. Two Wi-Fi modules coexist with two cellular modules identified as XMR2021EC25AFDL.
Intel lists D2W as the M.2 1216 version, 12×16×1.7 mm nominal; PCIe for Wi-Fi and USB for Bluetooth. Bluetooth bus capability does not mean enabled Bluetooth in this host.
Zipline-only integration uses authorized antennas and host labeling; 802.11n MIMO test mode is documented.

profiles.configuration: Nuro 2A98RDJZCGWA, documented in Camera Aggregator DVT2 / software 3.14. JODY-W3 R15 describes component-family capabilities; the Nuro filings establish the deployed restrictions. Exact ordering suffix, module memory and host processor are undisclosed.

facts.details: 2023 test filing identifies u-blox Jody W374, original XPYJODYW374, within the Nuro host.
JODY-W374 datasheet lists NXP 88W9098 / 88Q9098 alternatives. The filing does not resolve which silicon variant or ordering suffix Nuro installed.
August 2023 change disables Bluetooth 2402–2480 MHz and Wi-Fi 5260–5320 / 5500–5720 MHz in software. Adds an antenna type and cellular co-transmission with 2A98RDJZCGCA.
DVT2 test covers 5150–5250 MHz channels 36–48 and 5725–5850 MHz channels 149–165, using 802.11a/g/n/ac modes. Do not interpret the restriction as disabling all 5 GHz.
W374 supports PCIe or SDIO for Wi-Fi and UART for Bluetooth, with two antenna pins. These capabilities do not prove which host bus was wired or enable disabled Bluetooth.

profiles.configuration: Nuro 2A98RDJZCGCA, associated by the 2023 Camera Aggregator DVT2 filing with Quectel EG18-NA / XMR202002EG18NA. Component architecture uses EG18 Hardware Design v1.0. Optional/under-development interfaces are not treated as installed. Processor SKU and memory capacities remain undisclosed.

facts.details: Camera Aggregator filing identifies EG18-NA, with LTE FDD/TDD and W-CDMA operation. Exact regional bands remain those of the filing, not every EG18 variant.
Separate baseband, transceiver, RF front end and power-management blocks; no baseband part number disclosed.
LPDDR2 SDRAM and NAND flash appear in the block diagram; capacities are not supplied.
3.3–4.3 V, typically 3.8 V. The host’s 12 V input is a separate power domain.
USB 3.0/2.0, main/debug UART, two 1.8/3 V SIM interfaces in dual-SIM single-standby mode, and PCM. PCIe is marked under development in this revision and is not asserted as available.
Quectel AT commands; USB 2.0 firmware upgrade and DFOTA.

profiles.configuration: Exact automotive data-device test configuration, August 2023. Not a complete Nuro R2/R3 vehicle BOM or evidence of its autonomous-driving CPU. Host processor, RAM, storage and camera sensor models are not disclosed.

facts.details: Quectel EG18-NA cellular and u-blox Jody W374 Wi-Fi; Nuro module IDs 2A98RDJZCGCA and 2A98RDJZCGWA.
Separate u-blox NEO-M8T concurrent GNSS module; not assumed to be the cellular module’s internal receiver.
12 VDC in the test configuration; distinct from individual module supply rails.
Taoglas MA9906.A.007.dp, IP67 external antenna. The 5 GHz test lists two transmitting chains and 20/40/80 MHz modes.
August 2023 update disables Bluetooth and selected 5 GHz bands; the modules’ generic capability lists are broader than this host configuration.

profiles.configuration: April 2023 fifth-generation configuration. Historical component reference, not the sixth-generation RoboTruck. Exact main CPU/GPU SKU, RAM, storage, radio module and supply ratings are not disclosed.

facts.details: Ambarella CV2 camera processor; ruggedized Crystal main computing platform. The article does not identify a specific Crystal computer or main processor model.
Two Actuation Control Engines (ACE) handle safety control and the interface between autonomy and the truck chassis.
Eighteen sensors overall. Mirror-mounted SensorPods contain the autonomy-critical sensors, including forward LiDAR; the earlier roof-mounted pod is removed.
Power and data connectors use aviation-grade designs. Individual connector part numbers are not given.
ACE controllers support a safe fallback after a critical failure; this does not establish the operating-system version.

profiles.configuration: January 2024 sixth-generation design and January 2025 Atlas RoboTruck association. CPU/GPU SKU, RAM/storage capacities and LTE modem models remain undisclosed. Announced future CV3-AD integration is not treated as installed hardware.

facts.details: NVIDIA GPUs process perception data; Kodiak ACE is the independent high-integrity safety computer. Neither GPU nor ACE silicon part numbers are supplied.
Twelve cameras, four LiDAR sensors, six radars and emergency-sound microphones; replaceable, pre-calibrated SensorPods.
Redundant LTE communications links; carrier, band plan and modem SKU are not specified.
Two electrically isolated supply subsystems power computers, sensors, actuators and other electrical loads.
Three pneumatic brake actuators and two redundant ZF steering actuators.
Safety control can move the truck out of traffic after a critical failure.

January 2025 Atlas customer-owned RoboTrucks use the sixth-generation platform. The issuer filing links legacy Kodiak Robotics with Kodiak AI; that company relationship does not identify a truck generation by radio signal.

profiles.configuration: The 2021 commercially delivered Xuanyuan system and published ADCU Gen 1 reference. Journey 3 is an identified component, not proof that it is the only processor. Sensor models, radios, memory and vehicle powertrain vary or remain undisclosed.

facts.details: Inceptio states that the commercially delivered 2021 Xuanyuan system included Horizon Journey 3 chips.
Published control-unit rating is 245 TOPS, with automotive-grade redundancy; enclosure 414×294×100 mm. This total is not a Journey 3 single-chip rating.
ADCU Gen 1 is rated at 1.53 TOPS/W; no input voltage, battery capacity or actual operating draw is derived from that figure.
Modular electrical/electronic architecture separates hardware from software and provides a standardized SDK for vehicle adaptation.
Inceptio’s December 2025 technical retrospective identifies a first-generation mixture of Journey 3 and CV2 accelerators; counts and remaining controller components are not specified.

profiles.configuration: Gen 2 configuration announced December 2022 with planned Q4 2023 production, plus the manufacturer’s ADCU Gen 2 specification. The announcement alone is not proof every truck received it. RAM/storage, radio modules and full sensor BOM are not published here.

facts.details: Two Horizon Journey 5 chips, each rated up to 128 TOPS, for a 256-TOPS board. Uses Horizon’s Bayesian BPU architecture.
262 KDMIPS plus 256 TOPS; 380×246×75 mm enclosure. Expansion beyond 1,000 TOPS is a scalable architecture capability, not the base configuration.
Published cross-system synchronization is below 30 ns; physical connector and bus assignments are not supplied.
Published stack covers multi-view perception, ARC 2.0 planning/control and FEAD 2.0 fuel optimization. Software version installed on an individual truck is not established.
The December 2025 retrospective names Lyra as the second-generation controller and identifies an additional eight-core NXP processor alongside the two Journey 5 chips; exact NXP SKU is not given.

profiles.configuration: Manufacturer-published Robocar design reviewed November 2026. These are advertised configuration details, not a teardown or proof of delivery of any particular unit. Regional radio modules vary; RAM capacities and individual module part numbers are not fully disclosed.

facts.details: Eight NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor SoCs with Blackwell GPUs; each Thor is described with a 14-core Arm Neoverse V3 AE CPU.
Two TI TDA4VH processors, two NXP S32G399A processors and Renesas RH850 microcontrollers. TI units are described with eight Cortex-A72 cores; the NXP units combine Cortex-A53 and Cortex-M7 cores.
Samsung E1.A solid-state storage supports up to 19 TB. This is a supported maximum, not a guaranteed installed capacity.
Liquid thermal management and dual-power architecture protect the computing subsystem.
Renesas controller software uses Vector AUTOSAR.
Three independent 5G links using Qualcomm and Continental technology; region-specific module models are not identified.

One Halo and four Sentinel LiDARs, seventeen 17-MP exterior cameras, six Trinova radars and four external microphone arrays. Navigation combines GNSS/RTK, inertial sensors, wheel encoders and perception.
FEV-assisted VDU uses an NXP S32G chipset and AUTOSAR architecture; the page does not specify the VDU’s exact S32G suffix.
Published 845 V architecture and 112 kWh battery; dual-channel DC/DC and dual low-voltage backup batteries.
Steering uses redundant power, communication channels, controllers, motor windings and sensors.
OTA updates cover the VDU and vehicle subsystems. Oracle-backed data processing and training infrastructure is separate from onboard driving compute.

profiles.configuration: September 2024 commercial mining-truck architecture. Does not assign this hardware to highway prototypes, the AXL concept or every Scania model. CPU, RAM/storage, sensor/radio chip models and engine configuration are not disclosed.

facts.details: LiDAR, radar and GPS observe traffic, people and obstacles ahead and beside the truck.
Short-range V2X communication with other vehicles or objects; the article also uses the term C-V2X but supplies no radio SKU or frequency.
Decentralized driving software runs on the vehicle rather than requiring individual human driving commands.
Control-room support and a mobile 2 stop override device supplement onboard autonomy. Its transport protocol is not identified.

profiles.configuration: 2026 US product-page configuration, Standard Range. A fleet-connected electric truck is not, by itself, evidence of driverless capability. CPU, RAM/storage, battery kWh capacity, radio model and autonomy sensor BOM are not disclosed.

facts.details: Three electric motors; up to 800 kW drive power. Manufacturer-estimated range is 325 miles under its stated test conditions.
Electric power take-off supports up to 25 kW.
Tesla for Business supplies fleet/location/charge monitoring; OTA software updates and remote diagnostics are described.

profiles.configuration: 2026 US product-page configuration, Long Range. A fleet-connected electric truck is not, by itself, evidence of driverless capability. CPU, RAM/storage, battery kWh capacity, radio model and autonomy sensor BOM are not disclosed.

facts.details: Three electric motors; up to 800 kW drive power. Manufacturer-estimated range is 500 miles under its stated test conditions.
Electric power take-off supports up to 25 kW.
Tesla for Business supplies fleet/location/charge monitoring; OTA software updates and remote diagnostics are described.

profiles.configuration: Manufacturer’s early Star walkthrough, with a separately dated March 2025 HIS update. Cockpit silicon is not the autonomy CPU. The walkthrough is configuration-specific; no claim that every current Star has the same battery or electronics. RAM and storage remain undisclosed.

facts.details: Walkthrough identifies Qualcomm 8155 alongside the cabin screens and driver interface; it does not identify this as the HIS autonomy processor.
5G connectivity is described; modem SKU, bands and carrier are not supplied.
Camera and radar perception, an infrared camera, electronic mirrors, gesture and face-recognition interfaces are described. Component part numbers are absent.
Chassis-integrated battery, described as up to 466 kWh, and distributed electric drive. These are early walkthrough specifications, not universal model-year values.
Manufacturer describes 500-TOPS HIS compute with multi-sensor fusion, without naming the accelerator. This rating is separate from the cabin’s Qualcomm 8155.
March 2025 update describes L2-Pro deployment and continuing L4 research; it does not establish unrestricted driverless operation.

profiles.configuration: AiTrucker / ICC and highway-solution architecture, not one truck chassis BOM. CPU/GPU SKU, memory, radio modules, numerical power requirements and sensor model list are not disclosed. Roadside/cloud equipment is separate from onboard vehicle hardware.

facts.details: Automotive ICC controller supports scalable compute and sensor clock synchronization; manufacturer specifies an ASIL-D-oriented design without naming its processors.
Integrated BeiDou navigation/positioning chip; the exact part number is undisclosed.
Sensor, network and data interfaces plus a hardware-adaptation toolchain are described; no physical bus pinout is provided.
AiTrucker driving software and Trunk GO freight-network services support the highway offering.
CAFC coordinates a lead truck and autonomous followers through vehicle-road-cloud collaboration and V2X; no band or packet signature is established.

profiles.configuration: 2023-08-23 manufacturer brochure. One documented Fetch-family configuration; not a universal specification for every Fetch AMR. OEM and Research bases remain separate.

facts.details: Intel Core i7-9700E.
32 GB RAM and 256 GB SSD.
Intel AX200; brochure lists 802.11ax Wi-Fi and Bluetooth 5.1. A shared Intel module is not a model-specific broadcast identifier.
SICK TiM 571: 25 m range and 220° field of view.
Deka 8G22NF sealed lead-acid battery; nominal nine-hour runtime. Autonomous docking, approximately three hours to 90% charge.
DisplayPort, two USB 3.0 ports, Ethernet and four 10 W speaker channels; 73 mounting points. Rated payload 100 kg, speed up to 1.75 m/s.
Two Intel RealSense D435 cameras.
AUX1: 360 W, RS-485, runstop and USB. AUX2: 180 W, RS-485 and Ethernet; not connected to runstop.
Zebra Symmetry, REST API and PartnerAPI.

profiles.configuration: 2023-08-21 manufacturer brochure. One documented Fetch-family configuration; not a universal specification for every Fetch AMR. OEM and Research bases remain separate.

facts.details: Intel Core i7-9700E.
32 GB RAM and 256 GB SSD.
Intel AX200; brochure lists 802.11ax Wi-Fi and Bluetooth 5.1. A shared Intel module is not a model-specific broadcast identifier.
SICK TiM 571: 25 m range and 220° field of view.
Deka 8G22NF sealed lead-acid battery; nominal nine-hour runtime. Autonomous docking, approximately three hours to 90% charge.
DisplayPort, two USB 3.0 ports, Ethernet and four 10 W speaker channels; 73 mounting points. Rated payload 100 kg, speed up to 1.75 m/s.
Ubuntu Linux LTS, ROS, ROS Navigation, joystick teleoperation and calibration applications.

profiles.configuration: Coco 2 launched February 2026. These components do not describe the earlier human-guided Coco generation. Orin NX memory SKU, storage, radio module, sensor part numbers and battery capacity are undisclosed.

facts.details: NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX performs perception and driving computation locally.
Omniverse, Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab and Cosmos support simulation and training; these are not all claimed as onboard runtime components.
Cameras, solid-state LiDAR and GPS; individual sensor models are not identified.
Swappable battery and tires; published range 32 km, speed 21 km/h and maximum grade 30%.
Pilot Terminal provides navigation context, obstruction alerts and map annotation for human assistance.
End-to-end neural networks, precision mapping and human oversight.

profiles.configuration: 2022 monitoring robot described on page 35 of the manufacturer’s 2021 sustainability report. Not the later Sprayer or XT. CPU, memory, radio modules and numerical battery capacity are undisclosed.

facts.details: Cameras and sensors collect crop, pest, disease and weed observations for automated image analysis.
Solar-powered chassis measuring 2.5×2 m; manufacturer describes operation for up to three days with low solar input.
ALICE schedules tasks, interprets observations and selects movement timing and routes.

profiles.configuration: Sprayer configuration described after the 2023 US season. CPU, RAM, radio modules, camera models and battery capacity are not published here. Later boom and tank specifications are kept in their own configuration.

facts.details: Four solar panels supply the propulsion and spray systems.
Low-speed spray booms support targeted herbicide application; source describes usual 20-inch nozzle spacing.
ALICE supports spray-window recommendations and reports crop populations, weeds, insects, treatment maps and input usage.

profiles.configuration: May 2026 interview with Solinftec’s US commercial manager. Configuration-specific firsthand description; not the diesel-generator XT configuration. Processor, RAM/storage, radio and battery Wh remain undisclosed.

facts.details: Eight cameras identify weeds along the 40-foot boom; each camera controls three independent nozzles.
Solar panels charge a lithium-ion battery during operation.
56-gallon dual-tank system supplies the independently controlled nozzles.
ALICE AI performs crop/weed classification in real time.

profiles.configuration: T5 manual filed under FCC ID 2AZLQ-T5 in 2021. This 55 kg / 48 V 15 Ah configuration differs from later 12 Ah brochures. CPU, RAM, storage and radio chipset are not identified.

facts.details: Stereo vision, laser radar, image module and collision edge; two driven wheels and four supporting wheels.
Manual specifies 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi at 2412–2462 MHz. Band support is not a unique robot signature.
48 V / 15 Ah battery; listed rated power 40 W. Automatic or manual charging with 100–240 V AC charger input.
Touch display, speaker, emergency stop and four trays; manual rates 15 kg per layer and maximum travel speed 1.2 m/s.
Android desktop starts the PEANUT application, which manages routes, delivery and charging schedules.
FCC filing 2AZLQ-T5 identifies this T5 configuration; it is not a MAC address.

profiles.configuration: December 2021 supplier-confirmed MagicBag20 hardware. Exact Pandar/XT model numbers, main processor, memory, radio modules and battery specifications are not supplied. No later-generation sensor assignment is inferred.

facts.details: Hesai Pandar-series long-range and XT-series medium-range LiDAR provide complementary 360° coverage.

profiles.configuration: Manufacturer’s 2023-era delivery-vehicle description; hardware revision unnamed. Kept separate from the 2021 MagicBag20 supplier BOM. CPU, memory, radio and battery capacity are undisclosed.

facts.details: Vision and laser sensing; manufacturer claims 360° coverage within 150 m.
Published maximum speed 45 km/h and battery range 120 km; test conditions are not provided.
Published maximum payload 150 kg and cargo volume 540 L.
In-house L4 software/hardware architecture uses high-precision map localization and route planning.

profiles.configuration: April 2022 indoor delivery configuration. Not the outdoor sixth-generation Plus. CPU, memory, battery, radio modules and sensor part numbers are not disclosed.

facts.details: LiDAR, ultrasonic sensing and a depth camera detect obstacles and support localization.
IoT integration coordinates elevators and access control. Recipients receive a retrieval password by message/call; this does not establish an onboard cellular modem.
JD-developed localization and route planning navigate between floors and delivery destinations.

profiles.configuration: September 2026 supplier design-win announcement for the L4 Lone Wolf sixth-generation Plus vehicle. Planned integration, not proof every already-deployed JD vehicle uses this chip. RAM, storage, radios, battery and sensor BOM are not disclosed.

facts.details: Horizon Journey 6P; supplier rates one chip at 560 TOPS using the Nash BPU architecture.
The announced platform supports Transformer and BEV inference with multimodal sensor fusion.

profiles.configuration: April 2026 exhibition configuration and associated U-Drive architecture. CPU, memory, radio modules, sensor SKUs, battery capacity and tow rating are not disclosed.

facts.details: Electric chassis with published width of 1,355 mm; battery voltage and energy are not specified.
Demonstrated automatic trailer uncoupling for factory logistics.
Fifth-generation U-Drive / AI Driver software provides vehicle adaptation and redundant safety architecture.
Cloud dispatch and remote support complement vehicle perception, localization and planning. No transport protocol or radio band is established.

profiles.configuration: Shanghai 2025 manufacturer announcement; production was planned for 2027. A design reference, not a confirmed deployed-fleet BOM. Chip count, RAM, storage, radio modules and battery ratings are not disclosed.

facts.details: Horizon Journey 6P collaboration announced for Space and other L4 trucks; no dual-chip installation is established by this source.
Hesai AT1440 named for the planned integration.
Multiple battery configurations supported; CATL Qiji battery-swap network partnership announced.
Cabless chassis, customizable wheelbase and interchangeable cargo bodies for several freight types.
KargoBot Neutron uses end-to-end neural-network and reinforcement-learning methods.

profiles.configuration: June 2026 mass-production announcement for Taurus. Separate from Journey 3 and dual-Journey 5 predecessors. Installed RAM/storage capacity, modem, sensor part numbers and input voltage remain undisclosed.

facts.details: Single Horizon Journey 6M combines CPU, BPU and MCU; platform rated 137K DMIPS and 128 TOPS.
Integrated high-precision GNSS/INS module; supplier and module SKU are not given.
Air-cooled controller designed for prolonged operation at ambient temperatures up to 85°C; actual electrical draw is not supplied.
Transformer perception supports Truck Navigate-on-Autopilot. Manufacturer states ASIL-B functional safety and ISO 21434 cybersecurity certification.
Storage and transmission management handles weak network coverage; capacity and storage technology are not identified.

profiles.configuration: DrinkBot Pro manual V110323, linked by the manufacturer training site. CPU, RAM/storage, radio chipset, Wi-Fi bands and sensor part numbers are not disclosed. This does not establish specifications for every later BotristaPro revision.

facts.details: Wi-Fi supports software updates, menu downloads and remote troubleshooting; no model-specific broadcast signature is supplied.
Ethernet is recommended; touch interface selects recipes, size and sugar level.
Manual rates the unit at 110 V and 15 A.

Twelve ingredient tubes serve eight refrigerated and four ambient bag-in-box stores. Fourteen dispensing nozzles, a honeycomb blending cup and blender rinser form the beverage path; refrigerated lines extend to the nozzles.
Menu downloads, drink customization and cleaning/refill notifications are described in the operator manual.
Manufacturer specifies filtered cold water, minimum 40 psi, and a nearby drain.
Manufacturer training page links this DrinkBot Pro user manual and component tutorials.

profiles.configuration: Sally 2.0 manufacturer operator manual, mirrored by Parts Town. Not the unrelated Realbotix humanoid named Sally. Processor, RAM/storage and cellular modem SKU/bands are not disclosed.

facts.details: Manual specifies cellular connectivity and discourages Ethernet/Wi-Fi for this configuration.

Published rating: dedicated 120 V AC, 20 A, 60 Hz service. Refrigeration uses R134a. The manual also prints NEMA 5-15R; confirm the unit-specific installation requirement rather than reconciling that discrepancy by assumption.
15.6-inch tablet interface; optional 32-inch 720p LED ChowboticsTV. Payment terminal and receipt printer are described as options.
Twenty-two ingredient canisters feed a carousel, motor-arm and chute assembly. Outer and inner motors, guide rail and control panel are identified.
Refrigeration temperature LCD and software warnings report out-of-range temperature.
Tablet software manages bowl selection, ingredient customization and nutritional information.

profiles.configuration: Published configurable Makeline architecture. CPU, RAM/storage and exact sensor/RFID chipsets are not disclosed. Cabinet ratings are per module, not total line consumption; no Wi-Fi or RFID frequency is inferred.

facts.details: One to six ingredient dispensing cabinets, with denest and lift cabinets; hot, cold and ambient ingredient holding. Ten-inch touch HMI and cabinet light indicators.
Weight-based dispensing; RFID-equipped dispensers support configuration checks. Digitally regulated cabinet temperatures.
Manufacturer additionally identifies LiDAR and vision systems; models and optical specifications are unspecified.
Cat5e/6 RJ45 Ethernet; published bandwidth requirement 15 Mbps down / 10 Mbps up. Orders enter through API, POS integration or HMI.
208–240 V, 60 Hz, single phase. Denest/lift: 0.16 kW each; cold: 0.95 kW; hot: 2.25 kW; dry: 0.3 kW. Forced-air refrigeration uses R290.
Plating patterns can be updated across the fleet remotely; this does not identify a wireless transport.

profiles.configuration: Published kiosk architecture; the page combines specifications and Gen-3 preorder material without clearly assigning every rating to a revision. Main processor, memory, network hardware and camera models are undisclosed.

facts.details: Refrigeration, grill, bun toaster, assembly and boxed-product delivery are integrated into one cabinet. Published capacity is approximately 70 burgers per refill.
Built-in cameras support quality/security monitoring and live viewing; no camera sensor SKU is supplied.
Cloud monitoring covers inventory and performance; digital payment and menu configuration are supported. The page does not specify radio bands or network protocols.
The page lists 220 V / 11 A or 110 V / 22 A in one block, and 220 V / 30 A in another. A single revision-specific rating is not established; these must not be combined into one specification.
Integrated self-cleaning system; manufacturer states no external plumbing is required.

profiles.configuration: Supplier case study with Sweetgreen’s director of automation. Applies to the described Infinite Kitchen production configuration, not every earlier Spyce kitchen. Main CPU, RAM/storage, network hardware and input power are not identified.

facts.details: Teknic ClearPath-MC integrated servo units execute programmed position sequences locally. This identifies the motion-controller family, not the main application CPU or silicon SKU.
Servo-driven linkage grasps a bowl, rotates it through 720 degrees to mix, then returns it to the conveyor. Simple control inputs trigger stored moves.
Conveyor and automated ingredient tubes assemble bowls; supplier reports approximately 500 bowls per hour.
ClearPath integrates a high-resolution encoder with its brushless motor, drive electronics and motion controller.
Case study describes IP67 servo assemblies with M12 connectors; exact motor part numbers and pin assignments are not published.

profiles.configuration: August 2026 supplier-confirmed reference line, subsequently deployed at a customer site. Not assigned to historical Microfactory cells. CX5340 catalog options below are distinguished from the installation’s undisclosed configuration.

facts.details: Each cell uses a Beckhoff CX5340 Embedded PC; a separate, unspecified Beckhoff controller coordinates the line.
CX5340 uses a quad-core Intel Atom x6425RE at 1.9 GHz.
CX5340 catalog: 8 GB LPDDR4 standard, factory option 16 GB; CFast and microSD slots. Case study does not disclose installed RAM option or storage capacity.
EtherCAT connects motion and I/O. EL-series terminals, IP67 EP-series boxes, IO-Link peripherals and TwinSAFE/FSoE implement distributed control and safety.
Smart Skills supports 3D navigation, inspection and force control. Line equipment includes RFID readers; exact sensor models are unspecified.
Windows and TwinCAT 3; OPC UA Server links the control layer to proprietary orchestration and cloud monitoring with encryption.
CX5340 base includes two RJ45 ports up to 2.5 Gbit/s, four USB 3.1 ports and DisplayPort. Additional fieldbus interfaces are optional.
CX5340: 24 V DC, passive cooling and integrated one-second UPS. Catalog maximum draw 19 W, or 38 W while charging UPS; this is not total cell power.

profiles.configuration: Manufacturer’s A3 product listing and hardware-team demonstration. CPU, RAM/storage, robot-arm models, controller part numbers, radio modules and electrical ratings are not established by these sources. Bright Factory’s later CX5340 configuration is kept separate.

facts.details: Bright Robotic Cells, material feeders, manual stations and collaborative robots form configurable assembly lines.
Embedded real-time firmware runs the cells. Brightware orchestration can be deployed on premises or in enterprise cloud infrastructure, with bidirectional synchronization of production state.
Manufacturer describes software-driven assembly/inspection and product traceability; CPU/GPU servers mentioned in the demonstration are products being assembled, not identified robot controllers.

profiles.configuration: Configurable E80 laser-guided vehicle family. CPU, memory, radio chipsets, battery voltage/capacity and individual vehicle model are unspecified. SmartDect and stereo-vision features describe equipped configurations, not a verified retrofit to every historical LGV.

facts.details: Laser-guided navigation for pallet handling; proximity laser scanners and alarm systems protect the operating area.

Equipped vehicles communicate with worker tags to estimate position, speed and direction; published detection distance up to 50 feet. UWB chipset and operating frequency are not disclosed and this is not a unique passive signature.
Stereo-camera network and deep-learning processing reconstruct nearby people and obstacles in 3D; sensor and processor SKUs are unspecified.
Flash Battery lithium batteries and inductive charging are documented; daily battery monitoring is provided through Flash Data Center.
SM.I.LE80 manages fleet movement and intralogistics, integrates with plant ERP and supports remote supervision.
Configurable pallet forks, double-depth storage and side-by-side load handling connect vehicles with conveyors, storage and truck-loading systems.

profiles.configuration: Configurable AS/RS and published System Logistics Suite control architecture. Not a fixed bill of materials for every plant. PLC CPU model, server processor, RAM/storage, sensor part numbers and power ratings remain unspecified.

facts.details: PLC-based electrical and safety control sits below a material-flow controller, which communicates with warehouse management. Exact PLC model and processor are not named.
WCS/WMS/MFC connect with ERP, MES, yard and labor systems. SAP EWM-MFS integration uses bidirectional telegram interfaces to PLCs.
Manufacturer lists Zenon/WinCC visualization and TIA/E-Plan engineering; vehicle control, monitoring/analytics and virtual commissioning are available modules.

AS/RS configurations include stacker cranes, fast-rotation storage and miniload systems. Stacker cranes can use single/double-depth telescopic forks or multi-depth satellite trolleys; selection is project-specific.

profiles.configuration: Core picking configuration documented in 2026; one named system within the broad Berkshire Grey catalog entry. Not the BOM of every sorter or trailer unloader. CPU/GPU, memory, arm model, radio interfaces and power ratings are not disclosed.

facts.details: Vision evaluates item pose and grasp points. Vacuum/suction feedback checks grip security; sensor models are unspecified.
SpectrumGripper uses adaptive suction and quick-change cups for varied packaging; product sheet describes handling up to 6 kg.
BG Pilot combines perception, grasp selection, motion planning and orchestration; product-specific compute hardware is not named.
Configurations connect with AS/RS, AMRs, sorters, put walls and auto-baggers. AutoStore CarouselAI and VersaAI are named integrations, not evidence of identical internal hardware.

profiles.configuration: ASTI Ebot 350 manufacturer datasheet distributed by Europneumaq; table visually checked. CPU/safety-PLC model, RAM/storage, radio chipsets, battery voltage and capacity are not disclosed. Navigation and optional radio choices are configuration-dependent.

facts.details: Safety PLC supervises the protection system; no controller or processor part number is supplied.
QR-code, SLAM or magnetic navigation; two safety laser scanners, two emergency-stop buttons and QR/RFID reader functionality are described.
Wi-Fi; 4G and an additional radio-frequency system are optional. Bands, modules and unique broadcast identifiers are unspecified.
Lithium-ion battery with online charging. The advertised 24/7 operation depends on charging, not a 24-hour single-charge runtime.
Two USB ports, Ethernet and HMI. OPC PLC interface and ERP/MES/WMS integration; wired or wireless manual control.
Multidirectional platform, 350 kg payload; loaded speed 0.05–1.7 m/s and unloaded maximum 2 m/s.
SIGAT software interface.

profiles.configuration: JBT 2018 SGV system-overview configuration; historical manufacturer document remains indexed, but its original download may redirect to the successor FORMOVA site. Not a universal BOM for later vehicles. CPU, memory, radio-module and battery part numbers are undisclosed.

facts.details: Onboard mobile PC controls each vehicle. A separate SGV Manager server assigns tasks and coordinates plant equipment; processor models are unspecified.
Published WLAN options: IEEE 802.11a/b/g/n/ac. These shared standards do not identify a JBT vehicle by themselves.
Laser triangulation, natural-feature scanning, inertial, magnetic, wire and optical guidance are configuration alternatives; not a claim that each vehicle contains all sensors.
Electric vehicles report battery level; automatic charging or manual/automatic battery exchange depends on installation.
Factory LAN links WMS/WCS/ERP and PLC I/O. Vehicles include a color touchscreen and manual pendant; plant interfaces cover doors, conveyors and pickup/drop sensors.
SGV Manager client/server with SQL Server, historical records and hot backup. Layout Wizard defines routes; vendor support uses VPN.
Current FORMOVA vehicle catalog is linked separately; newer product specifications must not be backfilled into the 2018 configuration.

profiles.configuration: OSP grid-robot architecture with separately dated disclosures: 2016 radio design, 2017 battery description, 2021 engineering article and 2023 Erith RFID case study. Not an identical BOM across generations or the Chuck/Porter AMR fleet. CPU, memory, battery chemistry/capacity and final custom RFID chip are undisclosed.

facts.details: 2016 supplier disclosure: proprietary radio based on 4G principles in unlicensed 5 GHz spectrum, with ten updates per second per robot. This is not evidence of standard Wi-Fi interoperability or a unique passive signature.
Custom radio boards connect robots with warehouse base stations and the central control system; supplier describes simultaneous coordination of thousands of bots.
HID/CoreRFID describe custom grid-mounted tags for position tracking. Sentry 5706 / FIT 210 was an early trial; the final customized tag chipset and operating band are not identified.

2017 annual report, printed page 25: battery-powered grid robots with regenerative braking and roughly 200 W average consumption; charging under half an hour supports several hours of work. These ratings are not assigned to later 600 Series bots.
2021 engineering article describes continuous onboard data collection, cloud analysis and path-loss modelling for warehouse radio design. It does not disclose a public robot telemetry endpoint.

profiles.configuration: 600 Series configuration described in 2024 and 2026. Electronics, radio module, sensors and electrical ratings are not disclosed here; earlier OSP battery figures and patent example processors are not assigned to this model.

facts.details: Additive-manufactured lightweight chassis traverses the storage grid and retrieves totes from stacks up to 21 bins deep, delivering them to human or robotic pick stations.
Central orchestration and digital-twin planning coordinate bot movement and warehouse throughput. On-Grid Robotic Pick is a separate vision-guided arm on the grid, not an onboard arm in every bot.

profiles.configuration: MDX-1 / EVO Max V2 manufacturer manual; not the original MDX generation. Camera and radar configurations vary. CPU, RAM and radio-chip part numbers are undisclosed.

facts.details: 128 GB internal storage, approximately 64 GB available; microSD expansion up to 1 TB.
802.11a/b/g/n/ac/ax Wi-Fi: 2.4, 5.2 and 5.8 GHz region-dependent bands. Video link additionally supports 902–928 MHz in FCC/ISED regions.
GPS/Galileo/BDS/GLONASS, visual positioning and obstacle cameras. Six-direction 60–64 GHz radar or downward 24–24.25 GHz radar depends on regional hardware; RTK is optional.
Fusion 4T V2, Fusion 4N V2 or Fusion 4NZ-L V2 gimbal according to purchased variant; their camera specifications are not interchangeable.
ABX41-D: 4S Li-Po, 14.76 V, 9248 mAh, 136.5 Wh. MDX120W charger; battery hot swap requires prior app enablement.
Four motors; 1158CW/CCW propellers. EF9-3 Smart Controller V3 provides USB-C, USB-A and HDMI.
Smart Controller V3 runs Android 11-based software and Autel Enterprise; this is not the aircraft operating system.

profiles.configuration: Exact FCC 2AZKT71099000WIFI change-ID configuration. Specifications describe the Murata radio module, not a vehicle autonomy computer. Host CPU, RAM and storage are not established.

facts.details: Murata’s October 2021 authorization links Waymo FCC 2AZKT71099000WIFI to original FCC VPYLB1BN.
Murata LBEQ6ZZ1BN contains Marvell 88W8897 with a 40 MHz reference crystal; 802.11a/b/g/n/ac MIMO plus Bluetooth BR/EDR/LE. These shared chips and protocols are not unique Waymo identifiers.
2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands; 20/40 MHz 802.11n and up to 80 MHz 802.11ac channel widths. Channel availability depends on regional certification.
VDD33 nominal 3.3 V supplies the module RF circuitry, not the whole vehicle.
20.9 × 18.5 × 2.6 mm integrated transceiver; host connector and bus are not specified in this public manual.

profiles.configuration: FCC 2AZKT710-99000W, DEKRA March 2021 configuration. Component capabilities do not establish their enabled functions in Waymo firmware. Vehicle autonomy processor, total memory and host supply remain undisclosed.

facts.details: Two WWAN modules bearing FCC 2AX2UAR7592V1 and one WLAN module bearing VPYLB1BN.
Dual-band 802.11a/b/g/n/ac and Bluetooth 4.0. Report lists 2.4 GHz channels and 5 GHz UNII bands, with 80 MHz 802.11ac support.
The contained Murata LBEQ6ZZ1BN manual identifies Marvell 88W8897. It is radio silicon, not proof of Waymo’s main autonomy processor.

Carrier listing for the exact contained FCC ID identifies Rolling Wireless AR7592-1: ARM Cortex-A7 application core at 1.2 GHz. This is the modem module’s customer core, not the vehicle autonomy computer.
AR7592-1 supports LTE Cat 6, WCDMA and GSM; the carrier listing includes LTE B2/B4/B5/B12/B13. Enabled bands depend on the host configuration and carrier.
AR7592 supports GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou and QZSS. Public module capability does not prove Waymo uses it for primary vehicle positioning.
Carrier documentation lists UART and GPIO on the cellular module. Host-level pinout and external connectors are not disclosed.

profiles.configuration: Exact FCC 2AZKT710-60000W / RADE6 configuration, UL September 2021 report. Radar processing chip, memory and internal bus remain undisclosed. Millimeter-wave frequencies are outside ordinary Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and direct HackRF/RTL-SDR reception.

facts.details: FMCW automotive radar with digital beam-forming scanning antenna; LRES W6/W4, MRES and HRES operating modes.
Integral 29 × 2 × 1 mm antenna, reported gain 15.1 dBi. External test-interface boards are not treated as installed vehicle components.
Nominal 12 V DC external supply. Reported peak EIRP reaches 38.15 dBm in HRES; radiated power is not electrical consumption.
EUT firmware 382046355. The separately named test-laptop script is not the sensor’s onboard operating system.

profiles.configuration: Exact FCC 2AZKTRADE8C / RADE8C, UL March 2024 report. Not interchangeable with RADE6. Processor and memory are undisclosed; the radar requires suitable millimeter-wave receiving hardware.

facts.details: FMCW digital beam-forming radar with LRES W6/W4, MRES and HRES modes.
Four integral patch arrays radiate sequentially. Each array is 25 × 2 × 1 mm with reported gain 16 dBi.
Nominal 12 V DC car supply at test. HRES maximum measured average/peak EIRP: 33.45/43.98 dBm; not electrical consumption ratings.
Software/firmware revision cl@549997726 identifies the tested configuration; no onboard operating system or public telemetry interface is disclosed.

profiles.configuration: Exact FCC 2BML6P2EV3-0 / ZFC-P2EV3-0, HCT April 2026 radio report. This public report does not identify the CPU, RAM, storage or flight sensors; confidential exhibit listings are not component evidence.

facts.details: 802.11g/n HT20 at 2437 MHz, channel 6. Report describes SISO operation and tests two antenna chains individually; it does not establish simultaneous MIMO.
FPC dipole antenna, peak gain 6.5 dBi. Maximum measured conducted output 27.44 dBm (554.63 mW). These values apply to the tested configuration.
48 V supply in the equipment description; no battery chemistry, pack capacity or whole-aircraft consumption is specified.
Hardware 003A; firmware DRTU.07190.23.70.0. Engineering-mode tests fixed the transmit frequency; channel activity alone cannot identify a Zipline aircraft.
